lore:
The *Felis domesticus*, or the Common Hearth-Stalker, is a creature of dual nature. They dwell wherever humanity carves out a niche, from the soot-stained rafters of a wharfside tavern to the velvet divans of a queen’s solar. Though small, their predatory grace is peerless. They move like silk across stone, possessing a stillness that borders on the unnatural before erupting into a blur of needle-claws. Unlike the wolf, the cat hunts for more than mere sustenance; they are practitioners of a cruel play, often toying with their quarry to test the limits of the creature’s terror.

In the lore of the common folk, the cat is a bridge between worlds. It is widely whispered that they see the invisible threads of the ethereal, batting at spirits we cannot perceive. To harm one is to invite a decade of misfortune, for they are said to possess nine souls, each tethered to a different layer of the Great Beyond. Whether curled by a fire or prowling a moonlit battlement, the cat remains a silent observer of our follies—a miniature tiger masquerading as a friend.
